- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if price is falling sharply.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or low volatility, model tends to ignore trend; add 0.5–1.0% downward bias if no clear sentiment signal.
